subject: Streaming output gaps and WebSocket timeouts - escalation
messages:
From: Elaine Carter <elaine@novena.ai>
To: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: product@novena.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Streaming output gaps and timeouts affecting inference (urgent)

Hi Dylan,

We're seeing repeated, client-visible silent periods in streaming responses from Redwood's hosted endpoint over the last 36 hours. Symptoms:
- Long pauses (4-12s) in WebSocket/HTTP chunked streams mid-response that then resume; sometimes final completion never arrives and client sees a timeout.
- Error spikes (502/504) correlated with throughput surges.
- Impact: our real-time transcript and assistant session quality drops, customers are complaining.

I attached a compressed log sample and a pcap snippet of a failing session. We don't want to escalate to a contract-level incident, but this is materially affecting our product. Can you confirm you received the files and initiate a triage?

Session IDs (examples): sess_9f7c2, sess_a2d1b, sess_c3e9f

Thanks,
Elaine Carter
Head of Platform
Novena AI

From: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 09 Aug 2027 10:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Streaming output gaps and timeouts affecting inference (urgent)

Elaine, team — quick initial triage results after ingesting the logs you sent:
- We observed a pattern where reverse proxies (customer-edge LB + our internal proxy chain) are emitting idle timeouts around 10s during high-throughput bursts. This results in half-open TCP connections; the runtime's KV cache flush/emit resumes but the client-side socket sometimes sees an EOF or stalls.
- Error rate increase appears correlated with sudden request fan-out (many concurrent sessions) and a lowered chunk-flush frequency in the model driver under high load.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (short window):
1) Increase keepalive/idle timeout on the proxy layer from 10s -> 30s (temporary, low-risk).
2) Force more frequent chunk flushes (every 200ms) to ensure heartbeats during long generations.
3) Enable fallback mode: when chunking stalls, send a small "continuation" chunk every 500ms to keep TCP alive.

Request from Novena: please share one or two full request/response trace IDs (X-Request-ID) for any recent failures and confirm region. That will let us map to load balancer logs.

Attaching initial triage notes.
[attachment: redwood_triage_notes_0809.pdf]

—Dev

Redwood Inference

> Elaine — I opened HS-1234567 in our pipeline and created a short mutual action plan to keep you updated:
> - T+0-4h: Apply temporary proxy keepalive bump and enable chunk-heartbeat fallback (Dev/Markus)

I've applied the temporary proxy keepalive change in us-east-1 (non-disruptive) and flipped the chunk-heartbeat fallback on for Novena's tenant. Early telemetry (30m) shows:
- client-side observed stall rate down ~70% on sampled sessions
- 502/504 spike reduced but not fully resolved; we still see occasional stalls during peak concurrency.

Next steps I'm executing now:
- Roll a runtime patch to force a minimal flush interval (200ms) for long-running generations in your tenant (will be canaried to 5% of connections first).
- Collect additional traces and correlate with LB logs (please provide X-Request-IDs if you can).

If we see improvement over the next 4 hours, we can widen the canary and then make the config permanent. Will keep you posted.

-Markus
Markus Klein
